title: The Shepherd's Boy and the Wolf
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Shepherd's Boy was tending his flock near a village, and thought it would be great fun to hoax the villagers by pretending that a Wolf was attacking the sheep: so he shouted out, "Wolf! wolf!" and when the people came running up he laughed at them for their pains. He did this more than once, and every time the villagers found they had been hoaxed, for there was no Wolf at all. At last a Wolf really did come, and the Boy cried, "Wolf! wolf!" as loud as he could: but the people were so used to hearing him call that they took no notice of his cries for help. And so the Wolf had it all his own way, and killed off sheep after sheep at his leisure.
You cannot believe a liar even when he tells the truth.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Boy doing near the village?
options: Selling wool at the market
Building a new sheepfold
Tending his flock
Waiting for the shepherd to return

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Boy shout out to hoax the villagers?
options: "Wolf! wolf!"
"Help! Fire!"
"Run for your lives!"
"The sheep are lost!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Boy do when the villagers come running up?
options: He thanks them for their help
He hides so they cannot find him
He asks them to stay and watch the flock
He laughs at them for their pains

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the villagers discover each time they come running?
options: That the Boy had already driven the Wolf away
That they had been hoaxed, for there was no Wolf at all
That the flock had wandered off on its own
That the Boy had fallen asleep in the field

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens when a Wolf really does come at last?
options: The Boy runs to the village for help himself
The Boy chases the Wolf away alone
The Boy cries "Wolf! wolf!" as loud as he could
The Boy stays silent so the villagers rest

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do the villagers react to the Boy's final, real cries for help?
options: They take no notice of his cries
They come running faster than ever before
They send for the Boy's parents instead
They arrive too late to save any sheep

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why do the villagers ignore the Boy's cries when the Wolf finally comes?
options: They cannot hear him from that distance
They believe the Boy is a poor shepherd
They think the flock belongs to someone else
His past false alarms have taught them not to trust his warnings

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what allows the Wolf to kill the sheep "at his leisure"?
options: The Boy invites the Wolf closer to the flock
No one comes to drive him off, since the villagers ignore the warning
The sheep are too weak to run from him
The village has no one left to guard the flock

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Boy wanted to "hoax" the villagers?
options: To warn them honestly of real danger
To help them find the missing sheep
To trick them into believing something false
To teach them how to watch a flock

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A habit of lying destroys trust, even once the truth is being told
Villagers should always come running at the first cry for help
Wolves are cleverer than the shepherds who guard against them
A shepherd's boy should never be left alone with a flock

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Boy first shout "Wolf! wolf!"?
options: He truly sees a Wolf approaching the flock
He is testing whether the villagers can hear him
He wants the villagers to bring him food
He thinks it would be great fun to hoax the villagers

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many times does the Boy play this trick on the villagers?
options: Exactly one time
More than once
Every single day
Only after dark

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the real Wolf do to the flock once it arrives?
options: It scatters the flock without harming them
It is frightened away by the Boy's cries
It kills off sheep after sheep
It is driven off by the villagers at last

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Boy's laughter at the villagers reveal about how he views his trick?
options: He finds it amusing rather than something to feel guilty about
He is embarrassed and wants to apologize
He is afraid the villagers will punish him
He regrets bothering them so many times

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "took no notice" suggest about how seriously the villagers treat the final cry?
options: They discuss it carefully before deciding to ignore it
They believe the Boy but arrive too slowly to help
They send only a few villagers to check, just in case
They dismiss it immediately, expecting another false alarm

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Wolf killed sheep "at his leisure"?
options: Very quickly, before anyone could notice
Without hurry, since nothing stopped him
Only after the villagers gave permission
While the Boy watched and cheered him on

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A boy successfully warns the village about a real Wolf
A wolf is driven away before it can harm any sheep
A boy's false alarms leave him unheard when a real threat finally arrives
A village decides to stop keeping sheep altogether
